title: Difficult Airways, Special Patients, Difficult Patients and Difficult Contexts
content: Airways’ patency and protection, and the feasibility of ventilation, are necessary pre-requisites to have for oxygenation during the induction of a general anesthesia or before intubation in other contexts. The text presents a bulleted and holistic approach to the interwoven dynamics of the two fundamental variables for a safe airway management i.e. oxygenation and ventilation, which is intuitive, easy to grasp and rapid to apply on the scene. The ‘cannot ventilate, cannot intubate’ (CVCI) situation is analysed in its crucial variables and patterns. The concept of anticipated and unanticipated difficult airway is an useful theoretical leverage for the right mind gear. The recently emphasized term of ‘physiologically difficult airway’ is instead a misnomer as it rather refers to special patients at risk of desaturation, hypotension or cardiac arrest on preoxygenation and induction. Emphasis is in an approach on the airways, which is independent on the specialistic background. Control of the airways outdoors follows the same patterns of approach and decision making of indoors, but in difficult or unfriendly contexts.
